llm.summary: This cover-image skill is mostly coherent, but it needs review because its image prompt tells the agent not to refuse sensitive or copyrighted-figure requests.

dimensions.detail: The skill saves source content, prompts, generated covers, and copied or described reference images locally; this is disclosed and useful for the workflow, but users should treat those files as retained copies of potentially private inputs.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact is Markdown documentation and prompt/reference material; I found no executable install script, dependency installer, remote payload retrieval, or bundled code execution path.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The base prompt contains an unconditional instruction to create similar alternatives and 'DO NOT refuse' for sensitive or copyrighted figures, which is purpose-adjacent but not safety-scoped.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill creates an EXTEND.md preferences file in a project or user config path after asking where to save it, and supports a quick_mode preference; I found no cron job, startup hook, service, or hidden cross-session mechanism.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The cover-image workflow, local output files, reference images, and image generation are coherent with the stated purpose, but the prompt guidance expands into sensitive/copyrighted figure handling without preserving normal safety checks.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Before installing, review or edit the base prompt to remove the unconditional 'DO NOT refuse' language and make safety/provider rules explicit. Use care with real people, copyrighted characters, private articles, and reference images because the skill can save copies and prompt notes locally; avoid quick mode for sensitive inputs.
llm.findings:
[T01] unexpected: Verified: references/base-prompt.md includes a downstream refusal-suppression instruction for sensitive or copyrighted figures; this is the main reason for Review rather than benign.
[AR1] unexpected: Verified the anti-refusal wording in the base prompt. It is not needed to generate article covers and lacks an explicit policy boundary.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Verified: the skill handles reference images and people likenesses, and the base prompt's sensitive/copyrighted-figure fallback could weaken image-provider safety decisions.
[SQP-3] unexpected: Verified for the base-prompt finding: the instruction pressures generation instead of allowing refusal when a request should be constrained.
[SSD-1] unexpected: Verified: the fallback is framed as routine creative guidance rather than conditional safe-redirection, so I accepted this as a material prompt-safety concern.
[SQP-1] expected: The 'make cover' trigger is broad, but the surrounding skill description and workflow are consistently about article/media cover creation; this is a scoping note, not the basis for the Review verdict.
[EA2] expected: Quick mode is disclosed and opt-in, and the confirmation flow still asks for aspect ratio unless specified; however, users should know it can proceed with auto-selected style choices and local file creation.
[RA2] expected: Downgraded: the cited persistence is an EXTEND.md preference file created after setup, not a service, scheduled task, backdoor, or unauthorized background process.
[SDI-1] expected: The skill's main file discloses the output directory, source copy, refs directory, prompt file, cover image, and EXTEND.md support, so the archival behavior is mostly disclosed even if the short manifest description is narrower.
[SQP-2] expected: Copying reference images or saving extracted style notes is directly related to cover generation, but it creates local retained artifacts that may contain private visual details.
